# AGENTS.md — dsh-grok-workflow

This repository is the shared, durable memory and source of truth for the
`dsh-grok-workflow` plugin. Local and cloud agents MUST read this file before
changing code and MUST update the memory files before ending a work session.

## Start every task in this order

1. Read `AGENTS.md`.
2. Read `docs/knowledge/STATE.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, `HANDOFF.md`, `VALIDATION.md`.
3. Read `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/ACCEPTANCE.md`, `docs/knowledge/RESEARCH.md` when the task touches design, behavior, or verification.
4. Run `git status --short --branch`, inspect the latest commits, and check GitHub Issues/PRs relevant to the task.
5. Compare the memory with the actual code and test logs. Memory never overrides observed reality.

## Status vocabulary

Use these labels in memory files and reports:

- `CONFIRMED` — directly observed in source, a real command, or a real test.
- `HYPOTHESIS` — plausible but not yet verified.
- `NOT_RUN` — intentionally not executed yet.
- `BLOCKED` — cannot proceed without an external capability or decision.

Never write a claim as confirmed when only reasoning or a plan supports it.

## Truth rules for tests

- Every reported test result must name the exact command, environment, and result.
- A command that was not executed is `NOT_RUN`; a command that could not run is `BLOCKED` with the error.
- Unit tests must be deterministic and must not require an online model.
- Real DSH installation, loading, and interaction must be executed on this machine before being marked local-acceptance pass.
- Mock only expensive or nondeterministic boundaries (for example, a model or network). Keep the DSH tool registry, Loader, and plugin lifecycle real where the test claims to cover them.
- A child's self-report is not verification. Verification must inspect evidence, files, commands, or independent sources.

## Security and safety

- Never write API keys, tokens, passwords, `.env` contents, private keys, or unredacted credentials into source, tests, docs, Issues, commits, logs, or reports.
- Do not read or print credentials unless a task strictly requires a boolean presence check. Never echo their values.
- Never bypass DSH approval, sandbox, permission, or tool-policy controls.
- Never modify the DSH core repository to make this plugin work. Use documented extension points only.
- Do not publish to npm, create releases, or change repository visibility without explicit user authorization.
- Do not force-push, rewrite shared history, or push over an unknown remote. Inspect the remote first.

## Architecture invariants

- This plugin is an external DSH bundle. It must not fork or reimplement the DSH agent loop.
- The primary execution path is a workflow script executed by `ctx.workflowEngine`; child work is created through the engine's `agent()` hook, which uses DSH's subagent capability.
- Concurrency is bounded per workflow run: default 10, hard maximum 100. Retries are bounded: default 1, hard maximum 3. No unbounded loops.
- Verification is independent from execution and must validate evidence per acceptance criterion.
- Plugin unload must cancel/dispose active workflow runs and release all registrations. No ownerless background work.
- Keep the plugin inert when its bundle row is not mounted.

## Memory update cadence

Update memory immediately when a durable fact changes:

- New architecture/source fact → `docs/knowledge/RESEARCH.md`.
- Important choice with alternatives → `docs/knowledge/DECISIONS.md`.
- Bug, security issue, or failed test → `docs/knowledge/VALIDATION.md` and/or `STATE.md`.
- Meaningful phase completed → `docs/knowledge/STATE.md`.
- Hand-off to another agent → `docs/knowledge/HANDOFF.md`.

Before ending a session: update `STATE.md`, `HANDOFF.md`, and the relevant
validation/decision/research records, then commit and push shareable changes.

## Release and version discipline

- Record each user-visible feature, bug fix, or security fix under `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md`, in both English and Simplified Chinese.
- Do not bump the package version for every development commit. Bump `package.json` and `package-lock.json` together when preparing a release, and update the matching changelog section.
- Use version tags in the form `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. Publish only from a merged `main` commit after CI passes.
- The Release workflow must validate the tag against `package.json`, run tests, verify committed `lib/` artifacts, require matching changelog notes, and only then create a GitHub Release.
- Never move or overwrite a published tag. A GitHub Release and Git history help recovery but are not a substitute for an independent repository backup. Never commit credentials or private runtime data.

## GitHub coordination protocol

Use Issue `[COORDINATION] Cloud ↔ Local Agent` for task assignment and status.
Use PRs for reviewable code. Every status comment must use this block:

```text
FROM: local | cloud
TO: cloud | both | local
TASK: #<issue-number>
BASE_COMMIT: <sha>
WORK_COMMIT: <sha-or-none>
CHANGES: <actual changes>
TESTS_RUN: <actual commands>
TEST_RESULTS: PASS | FAIL | NOT_RUN
LOCAL_RUNTIME_VERIFIED: yes | no
BLOCKERS: <specific blocker or none>
NEXT_ACTION: <one clear next action>
```

If a push failed, say which files are unsynced and why. Never imply that a
remote agent can see local-only commits.

This repository is the shared, durable memory and source of truth for the
`dsh-grok-workflow` plugin. Local and cloud agents MUST read this file before
changing code and MUST update the memory files before ending a work session.

## Start every task in this order

1. Read `AGENTS.md`.
2. Read `docs/knowledge/STATE.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, `HANDOFF.md`, `VALIDATION.md`.
3. Read `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/ACCEPTANCE.md`, `docs/knowledge/RESEARCH.md` when the task touches design, behavior, or verification.
4. Run `git status --short --branch`, inspect the latest commits, and check GitHub Issues/PRs relevant to the task.
5. Compare the memory with the actual code and test logs. Memory never overrides observed reality.

## Status vocabulary

Use these labels in memory files and reports:

- `CONFIRMED` — directly observed in source, a real command, or a real test.
- `HYPOTHESIS` — plausible but not yet verified.
- `NOT_RUN` — intentionally not executed yet.
- `BLOCKED` — cannot proceed without an external capability or decision.

Never write a claim as confirmed when only reasoning or a plan supports it.

## Truth rules for tests

- Every reported test result must name the exact command, environment, and result.
- A command that was not executed is `NOT_RUN`; a command that could not run is `BLOCKED` with the error.
- Unit tests must be deterministic and must not require an online model.
- Real DSH installation, loading, and interaction must be executed on this machine before being marked local-acceptance pass.
- Mock only expensive or nondeterministic boundaries (for example, a model or network). Keep the DSH tool registry, Loader, and plugin lifecycle real where the test claims to cover them.
- A child's self-report is not verification. Verification must inspect evidence, files, commands, or independent sources.

## Security and safety

- Never write API keys, tokens, passwords, `.env` contents, private keys, or unredacted credentials into source, tests, docs, Issues, commits, logs, or reports.
- Do not read or print credentials unless a task strictly requires a boolean presence check. Never echo their values.
- Never bypass DSH approval, sandbox, permission, or tool-policy controls.
- Never modify the DSH core repository to make this plugin work. Use documented extension points only.
- Do not publish to npm, create releases, or change repository visibility without explicit user authorization.
- Do not force-push, rewrite shared history, or push over an unknown remote. Inspect the remote first.

## Architecture invariants

- This plugin is an external DSH bundle. It must not fork or reimplement the DSH agent loop.
- The primary execution path is a workflow script executed by `ctx.workflowEngine`; child work is created through the engine's `agent()` hook, which uses DSH's subagent capability.
- Concurrency is bounded per workflow run: default 10, hard maximum 100. Retries are bounded: default 1, hard maximum 3. No unbounded loops.
- Verification is independent from execution and must validate evidence per acceptance criterion.
- Plugin unload must cancel/dispose active workflow runs and release all registrations. No ownerless background work.
- Keep the plugin inert when its bundle row is not mounted.

## Memory update cadence

Update memory immediately when a durable fact changes:

- New architecture/source fact → `docs/knowledge/RESEARCH.md`.
- Important choice with alternatives → `docs/knowledge/DECISIONS.md`.
- Bug, security issue, or failed test → `docs/knowledge/VALIDATION.md` and/or `STATE.md`.
- Meaningful phase completed → `docs/knowledge/STATE.md`.
- Hand-off to another agent → `docs/knowledge/HANDOFF.md`.

Before ending a session: update `STATE.md`, `HANDOFF.md`, and the relevant
validation/decision/research records, then commit and push shareable changes.

## Release and version discipline

- Record each user-visible feature, bug fix, or security fix under `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md`, in both English and Simplified Chinese.
- Do not bump the package version for every development commit. Bump `package.json` and `package-lock.json` together when preparing a release, and update the matching changelog section.
- Use version tags in the form `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. Publish only from a merged `main` commit after CI passes.
- The Release workflow must validate the tag against `package.json`, run tests, verify committed `lib/` artifacts, require matching changelog notes, and only then create a GitHub Release.
- Never move or overwrite a published tag. A GitHub Release and Git history help recovery but are not a substitute for an independent repository backup. Never commit credentials or private runtime data.

## GitHub coordination protocol

Use Issue `[COORDINATION] Cloud ↔ Local Agent` for task assignment and status.
Use PRs for reviewable code. Every status comment must use this block:

```text
FROM: local | cloud
TO: cloud | both | local
TASK: #<issue-number>
BASE_COMMIT: <sha>
WORK_COMMIT: <sha-or-none>
CHANGES: <actual changes>

If a push failed, say which files are unsynced and why. Never imply that a
remote agent can see local-only commits.

# AGENTS.md — dsh-grok-workflow

This repository is the shared, durable memory and source of truth for the
`dsh-grok-workflow` plugin. Local and cloud agents MUST read this file before
changing code and MUST update the memory files before ending a work session.

## Start every task in this order

1. Read `AGENTS.md`.
2. Read `docs/knowledge/STATE.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, `HANDOFF.md`, `VALIDATION.md`.
3. Read `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/ACCEPTANCE.md`, `docs/knowledge/RESEARCH.md` when the task touches design, behavior, or verification.
4. Run `git status --short --branch`, inspect the latest commits, and check GitHub Issues/PRs relevant to the task.
5. Compare the memory with the actual code and test logs. Memory never overrides observed reality.

## Status vocabulary

Use these labels in memory files and reports:

- `CONFIRMED` — directly observed in source, a real command, or a real test.
- `HYPOTHESIS` — plausible but not yet verified.
- `NOT_RUN` — intentionally not executed yet.
- `BLOCKED` — cannot proceed without an external capability or decision.

Never write a claim as confirmed when only reasoning or a plan supports it.

## Truth rules for tests

- Every reported test result must name the exact command, environment, and result.
- A command that was not executed is `NOT_RUN`; a command that could not run is `BLOCKED` with the error.
- Unit tests must be deterministic and must not require an online model.
- Real DSH installation, loading, and interaction must be executed on this machine before being marked local-acceptance pass.
- Mock only expensive or nondeterministic boundaries (for example, a model or network). Keep the DSH tool registry, Loader, and plugin lifecycle real where the test claims to cover them.
- A child's self-report is not verification. Verification must inspect evidence, files, commands, or independent sources.

## Security and safety

- Never write API keys, tokens, passwords, `.env` contents, private keys, or unredacted credentials into source, tests, docs, Issues, commits, logs, or reports.
- Do not read or print credentials unless a task strictly requires a boolean presence check. Never echo their values.
- Never bypass DSH approval, sandbox, permission, or tool-policy controls.
- Never modify the DSH core repository to make this plugin work. Use documented extension points only.
- Do not publish to npm, create releases, or change repository visibility without explicit user authorization.
- Do not force-push, rewrite shared history, or push over an unknown remote. Inspect the remote first.

## Architecture invariants

# AGENTS.md — dsh-grok-workflow

This repository is the shared, durable memory and source of truth for the
`dsh-grok-workflow` plugin. Local and cloud agents MUST read this file before
changing code and MUST update the memory files before ending a work session.

## Start every task in this order

1. Read `AGENTS.md`.
2. Read `docs/knowledge/STATE.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, `HANDOFF.md`, `VALIDATION.md`.
3. Read `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/ACCEPTANCE.md`, `docs/knowledge/RESEARCH.md` when the task touches design, behavior, or verification.
4. Run `git status --short --branch`, inspect the latest commits, and check GitHub Issues/PRs relevant to the task.
5. Compare the memory with the actual code and test logs. Memory never overrides observed reality.

## Status vocabulary

Use these labels in memory files and reports:

- `CONFIRMED` — directly observed in source, a real command, or a real test.
- `HYPOTHESIS` — plausible but not yet verified.
- `NOT_RUN` — intentionally not executed yet.
- `BLOCKED` — cannot proceed without an external capability or decision.

Never write a claim as confirmed when only reasoning or a plan supports it.

## Truth rules for tests

- Every reported test result must name the exact command, environment, and result.
- A command that was not executed is `NOT_RUN`; a command that could not run is `BLOCKED` with the error.
- Unit tests must be deterministic and must not require an online model.
- Real DSH installation, loading, and interaction must be executed on this machine before being marked local-acceptance pass.
- Mock only expensive or nondeterministic boundaries (for example, a model or network). Keep the DSH tool registry, Loader, and plugin lifecycle real where the test claims to cover them.
- A child's self-report is not verification. Verification must inspect evidence, files, commands, or independent sources.

## Security and safety

- Never write API keys, tokens, passwords, `.env` contents, private keys, or unredacted credentials into source, tests, docs, Issues, commits, logs, or reports.
- Do not read or print credentials unless a task strictly requires a boolean presence check. Never echo their values.
- Never bypass DSH approval, sandbox, permission, or tool-policy controls.
- Never modify the DSH core repository to make this plugin work. Use documented extension points only.
- Do not publish to npm, create releases, or change repository visibility without explicit user authorization.
- Do not force-push, rewrite shared history, or push over an unknown remote. Inspect the remote first.

## Architecture invariants

- This plugin is an external DSH bundle. It must not fork or reimplement the DSH agent loop.
- The primary execution path is a workflow script executed by `ctx.workflowEngine`; child work is created through the engine's `agent()` hook, which uses DSH's subagent capability.
- Concurrency is bounded per workflow run: default 10, hard maximum 100. Retries are bounded: default 1, hard maximum 3. No unbounded loops.
- Verification is independent from execution and must validate evidence per acceptance criterion.
- Plugin unload must cancel/dispose active workflow runs and release all registrations. No ownerless background work.
- Keep the plugin inert when its bundle row is not mounted.

## Memory update cadence

Update memory immediately when a durable fact changes:

- New architecture/source fact → `docs/knowledge/RESEARCH.md`.
- Important choice with alternatives → `docs/knowledge/DECISIONS.md`.
- Bug, security issue, or failed test → `docs/knowledge/VALIDATION.md` and/or `STATE.md`.
- Meaningful phase completed → `docs/knowledge/STATE.md`.
- Hand-off to another agent → `docs/knowledge/HANDOFF.md`.

Before ending a session: update `STATE.md`, `HANDOFF.md`, and the relevant
validation/decision/research records, then commit and push shareable changes.

## Release and version discipline

- Record each user-visible feature, bug fix, or security fix under `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md`, in both English and Simplified Chinese.
- Do not bump the package version for every development commit. Bump `package.json` and `package-lock.json` together when preparing a release, and update the matching changelog section.
- Use version tags in the form `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. Publish only from a merged `main` commit after CI passes.
- The Release workflow must validate the tag against `package.json`, run tests, verify committed `lib/` artifacts, require matching changelog notes, and only then create a GitHub Release.
- Never move or overwrite a published tag. A GitHub Release and Git history help recovery but are not a substitute for an independent repository backup. Never commit credentials or private runtime data.

## GitHub coordination protocol

Use Issue `[COORDINATION] Cloud ↔ Local Agent` for task assignment and status.
Use PRs for reviewable code. Every status comment must use this block:

```text
FROM: local | cloud
TO: cloud | both | local
TASK: #<issue-number>
BASE_COMMIT: <sha>
WORK_COMMIT: <sha-or-none>
CHANGES: <actual changes>
TESTS_RUN: <actual commands>
TEST_RESULTS: PASS | FAIL | NOT_RUN
LOCAL_RUNTIME_VERIFIED: yes | no
BLOCKERS: <specific blocker or none>

```

If a push failed, say which files are unsynced and why. Never imply that a
remote agent can see local-only commits.

function.name: workflow
function.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

# AGENTS.md — dsh-grok-workflow

This repository is the shared, durable memory and source of truth for the
`dsh-grok-workflow` plugin. Local and cloud agents MUST read this file before
changing code and MUST update the memory files before ending a work session.

## Start every task in this order

1. Read `AGENTS.md`.
2. Read `docs/knowledge/STATE.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, `HANDOFF.md`, `VALIDATION.md`.
3. Read `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/ACCEPTANCE.md`, `docs/knowledge/RESEARCH.md` when the task touches design, behavior, or verification.
4. Run `git status --short --branch`, inspect the latest commits, and check GitHub Issues/PRs relevant to the task.
5. Compare the memory with the actual code and test logs. Memory never overrides observed reality.

## Status vocabulary

Use these labels in memory files and reports:

- `CONFIRMED` — directly observed in source, a real command, or a real test.
- `HYPOTHESIS` — plausible but not yet verified.
- `NOT_RUN` — intentionally not executed yet.
- `BLOCKED` — cannot proceed without an external capability or decision.

Never write a claim as confirmed when only reasoning or a plan supports it.

## Truth rules for tests

- Every reported test result must name the exact command, environment, and result.
- A command that was not executed is `NOT_RUN`; a command that could not run is `BLOCKED` with the error.
- Unit tests must be deterministic and must not require an online model.
- Real DSH installation, loading, and interaction must be executed on this machine before being marked local-acceptance pass.
- Mock only expensive or nondeterministic boundaries (for example, a model or network). Keep the DSH tool registry, Loader, and plugin lifecycle real where the test claims to cover them.
- A child's self-report is not verification. Verification must inspect evidence, files, commands, or independent sources.

## Security and safety

- Never write API keys, tokens, passwords, `.env` contents, private keys, or unredacted credentials into source, tests, docs, Issues, commits, logs, or reports.
- Do not read or print credentials unless a task strictly requires a boolean presence check. Never echo their values.
- Never bypass DSH approval, sandbox, permission, or tool-policy controls.
- Never modify the DSH core repository to make this plugin work. Use documented extension points only.
- Do not publish to npm, create releases, or change repository visibility without explicit user authorization.
- Do not force-push, rewrite shared history, or push over an unknown remote. Inspect the remote first.

## Architecture invariants

- This plugin is an external DSH bundle. It must not fork or reimplement the DSH agent loop.
- The primary execution path is a workflow script executed by `ctx.workflowEngine`; child work is created through the engine's `agent()` hook, which uses DSH's subagent capability.
- Concurrency is bounded per workflow run: default 10, hard maximum 100. Retries are bounded: default 1, hard maximum 3. No unbounded loops.
- Verification is independent from execution and must validate evidence per acceptance criterion.
- Plugin unload must cancel/dispose active workflow runs and release all registrations. No ownerless background work.
- Keep the plugin inert when its bundle row is not mounted.

## Memory update cadence

Update memory immediately when a durable fact changes:

- New architecture/source fact → `docs/knowledge/RESEARCH.md`.
- Important choice with alternatives → `docs/knowledge/DECISIONS.md`.
- Bug, security issue, or failed test → `docs/knowledge/VALIDATION.md` and/or `STATE.md`.
- Meaningful phase completed → `docs/knowledge/STATE.md`.
- Hand-off to another agent → `docs/knowledge/HANDOFF.md`.

Before ending a session: update `STATE.md`, `HANDOFF.md`, and the relevant
validation/decision/research records, then commit and push shareable changes.

## Release and version discipline

- Record each user-visible feature, bug fix, or security fix under `[Unreleased]` in `CHANGELOG.md`, in both English and Simplified Chinese.
- Do not bump the package version for every development commit. Bump `package.json` and `package-lock.json` together when preparing a release, and update the matching changelog section.
- Use version tags in the form `vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH`. Publish only from a merged `main` commit after CI passes.
- The Release workflow must validate the tag against `package.json`, run tests, verify committed `lib/` artifacts, require matching changelog notes, and only then create a GitHub Release.
- Never move or overwrite a published tag. A GitHub Release and Git history help recovery but are not a substitute for an independent repository backup. Never commit credentials or private runtime data.

## GitHub coordination protocol

Use Issue `[COORDINATION] Cloud ↔ Local Agent` for task assignment and status.
Use PRs for reviewable code. Every status comment must use this block:

```text
FROM: local | cloud
TO: cloud | both | local
TASK: #<issue-number>
BASE_COMMIT: <sha>
WORK_COMMIT: <sha-or-none>
CHANGES: <actual changes>
TESTS_RUN: <actual commands>
TEST_RESULTS: PASS | FAIL | NOT_RUN
LOCAL_RUNTIME_VERIFIED: yes | no
BLOCKERS: <specific blocker or none>
NEXT_ACTION: <one clear next action>
```

If a push failed, say which files are unsynced and why. Never imply that a
remote agent can see local-only commits.

# AGENTS.md — dsh-grok-workflow

This repository is the shared, durable memory and source of truth for the
`dsh-grok-workflow` plugin. Local and cloud agents MUST read this file before

## Start every task in this order

1. Read `AGENTS.md`.
2. Read `docs/knowledge/STATE.md`, `DECISIONS.md`, `HANDOFF.md`, `VALIDATION.md`.
3. Read `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `docs/ACCEPTANCE.md`, `docs/knowledge/RESEARCH.md` when the task touches design, behavior, or verification.
4. Run `git status --short --branch`, inspect the latest commits, and check GitHub Issues/PRs relevant to the task.
5. Compare the memory with the actual code and test logs. Memory never overrides observed reality.

## Status vocabulary

Use these labels in memory files and reports:

- `CONFIRMED` — directly observed in source, a real command, or a real test.
- `HYPOTHESIS` — plausible but not yet verified.
- `NOT_RUN` — intentionally not executed yet.
- `BLOCKED` — cannot proceed without an external capability or decision.

Never write a claim as confirmed when only reasoning or a plan supports it.

## Truth rules for tests

- Every reported test result must name the exact command, environment, and result.
- A command that was not executed is `NOT_RUN`; a command that could not run is `BLOCKED` with the error.
- Unit tests must be deterministic and must not require an online model.
- Real DSH installation, loading, and interaction must be executed on this machine before being marked local-acceptance pass.
- Mock only expensive or nondeterministic boundaries (for example, a model or network). Keep the DSH tool registry, Loader, and plugin lifecycle real where the test claims to cover them.
- A child's self-report is not verification. Verification must inspect evidence, files, commands, or independent sources.

## Security and safety

- Never write API keys, tokens, passwords, `.env` contents, private keys, or unredacted credentials into source, tests, docs, Issues, commits, logs, or reports.
- Do not read or print credentials unless a task strictly requires a boolean presence check. Never echo their values.
- Never bypass DSH approval, sandbox, permission, or tool-policy controls.
- Never modify the DSH core repository to make this plugin work. Use documented extension points only.
- Do not publish to npm, create releases, or change repository visibility without explicit user authorization.
- Do not force-push, rewrite shared history, or push over an unknown remote. Inspect the remote first.

## Architecture invariants

- This plugin is an external DSH bundle. It must not fork or reimplement the DSH agent loop.
- The primary execution path is a workflow script executed by `ctx.workflowEngine`; child work is created through the engine's `agent()` hook, which uses DSH's subagent capability.
- Concurrency is bounded per workflow run: default 10, hard maximum 100. Retries are bounded: default 1, hard maximum 3. No unbounded loops.
- Verification is independent from execution and must validate evidence per acceptance criterion.
- Plugin unload must cancel/dispose active workflow runs and release all registrations. No ownerless background work.
- Keep the plugin inert when its bundle row is not mounted.

Update memory immediately when a durable fact changes:

- New architecture/source fact → `docs/knowledge/RESEARCH.md`.
- Important choice with alternatives → `docs/knowledge/DECISIONS.md`.
- Bug, security issue, or failed test → `docs/knowledge/VALIDATION.md` and/or `STATE.md`.

FROM: local | cloud

function.name: workflow
function.description:
Run a JavaScript workflow script that orchestrates subagents at scale. Use this for work that fans out across many independent pieces — an audit over many files, a migration, multi-angle research, adversarial verification of findings — where you write the orchestration as a script instead of delegating turn by turn.

Script-body hooks:
- `agent(prompt, opts?): Promise<any>` — run one subagent to completion. Without `opts.schema` it resolves to the child's final text; with `opts.schema` (an object-rooted JSON Schema using ONLY type/properties/required/additionalProperties/items/enum/const/oneOf) it resolves to the validated object. Resolves `null` when the child fails (filter with `.filter(Boolean)`). Other opts: `label` (display), `phase` (progress group), and independent `provider`/`model` LLM target overrides.
- `pipeline(items, ...stages): Promise<any[]>` — run each item through the stages independently with NO barrier between stages (prefer this for multi-stage work). Each stage receives `(prev, item, index)`. A stage throw drops that ITEM to `null` and skips its remaining stages.
- `parallel(thunks): Promise<any[]>` — run zero-argument functions concurrently and await ALL of them (a barrier; use only when a stage genuinely needs every prior result together). A throwing thunk resolves to `null`.
- `phase(title)` — start a progress phase; `log(message)` — narrate progress; `args` — the tool call's `args` input, verbatim.

Misused hooks (bad arguments, unknown options, unsupported schemas, tripped caps) end the whole script instead of producing `null`. The script has no filesystem, network, timer, or Node.js APIs; the agents do the work.

script.description: The plain JavaScript body, not TypeScript and without an `export const meta` statement; top-level await is allowed. End with `return <value>`; the JSON-serializable value is this tool's result.

meta.description: The workflow identity as plain JSON, not code.

name.description: Short kebab-case workflow name.

description.description: One-line description of what the workflow does.

whenToUse.description: Optional guidance on when this workflow applies.

phases.description: Optional phase declarations matched by phase() calls.

title.description: The phase title phase() calls match by exact string.

detail.description: Optional one-line description of the phase.

provider.description: Optional provider override this phase is expected to use.

model.description: Optional model override this phase is expected to use.

args.description: Optional JSON input exposed to the script as the `args` global (wrap a bare list as a field, e.g. {"files": [...]}).

run_in_background.description: Run as a background job: return a job id immediately instead of waiting; the return value arrives with the completion notice.

cd.description: Existing directory to enter. Omit to read the current directory.

function.name: write
function.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend. Provide `file_path` before `content` in the arguments.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.
